page: Vultr voc-s-16c-128gb-2560s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core. Operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled directly with the instance, providing 2560 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. No GPU accelerators are present on this server.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong memory subsystem capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier status in large-block memory write bandwidth and strong performance in large-block memory read bandwidth and Passmark memory scores. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is also strong, placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput remain in the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside substantial bundled NVMe storage, making it a cost-efficient choice for workloads requiring large memory footprints without the overhead of standalone storage attachments. The hardware profile is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, caching layers, software compilation, and medium-scale web serving.
description: Vultr voc-s-16c-128gb-2560s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 8 physical cores. It features 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high 8.0 GB per core ratio, and includes 2560 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results highlight top-tier performance in large-block memory write bandwidth and strong capabilities in memory read bandwidth and single-core CPU execution. While multi-core CPU and database operations perform in the average tier, the high memory density and fast local storage make this instance highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads. It is well-suited for database hosting, caching layers, and software compilation.
